compareCandidate.label: Addition vs. multiplication
compareCandidate.description: Addition joins any groups — equal or not (3 + 4). Multiplication joins equal groups only, as repeated addition (3 × 4 = 4 + 4 + 4).

processes: Combining sets to find a total
plainLanguageExplanation: Addition is putting two or more groups together and finding the total. If you have 3 red marbles and 4 blue marbles, addition tells you there are 7 marbles in all. The groups being added are called addends, and the answer is the sum. There are clever ways to add beyond just counting: counting on (start at 3 and count four more), and column addition (line the numbers up by place value and add ones, tens, and hundreds — regrouping when a column passes nine). Addition is commutative: 3 + 4 gives the same total as 4 + 3. Addition is also the opposite operation of subtraction, which is why 7 − 3 checks 3 + 4.

whyItMatters: Addition is everywhere: buying groceries, adding scores, measuring lengths, and combining data. It is also the doorway to subtraction, multiplication, and division, so getting fluent with adding sets and sums makes every later operation easier.
didYouKnow: The '+' plus sign was first used in the 1300s as a shorthand for 'and' — it literally comes from writing 'et' (Latin for and) quickly until it became a cross.
compareReason: Addition and multiplication look similar but behave differently — comparing equal-group vs. any-group joining clarifies when to use each.
